findings.what: The shipped A4 arm's comment and fixture do not actually discriminate role-counting from base-name counting, and its 'two passes never duplicate a member name' assertion runs over a board where NO pass grows anything.
findings.where: packages/mpd-cellwork-plugin/test/elastic-seats.test.ts — test 'F1 A4: maxPerRole counts SEATS BY ROLE, and two passes never duplicate a member name'
findings.why: The comment says base counting would count only one seat for 'SE', but baseSeatName('SE-2') is 'SE' and baseSeatName('SE') is 'SE', so the old base rule also counts 2 in that fixture; the arm only fails pre-fix because the old code refused earlier on role resolution. The idempotency half never exercises a grown seat across passes, so a regression that raised a second seat on the pass after a growth would not redden it. The behaviour itself is correct and was verified independently (probe A4 and probe A2 second pass).
findings.direction: Add a canonical-named seat ('Senior Engineer') to the A4 fixture so base count (1) and role count (2) diverge, and add a second pass over a board where the first pass grew a seat; correct the comment.

findings.what: Stale wording still describes the OLD cap subject ('one base role') after the contract corrected it to the resolved role.
findings.where: packages/mpd-cellwork-plugin/src/config.ts — field doc comment on the CellworkConfig maxPerRole field; packages/mpd-cellwork-plugin/src/staging.ts — the planning prompt sentence 'at most `cellwork.seats.maxPerRole` (N) seats per base role'
findings.why: These are agent-facing instructions a planning seat reads; they now contradict §3.6 and docs/cellwork.md ('counts seats OF the resolved role'). A9 is docs-scoped so this is not a criterion failure, but the text is user/agent-visible.
findings.direction: Reword both to 'seats of one resolved role' (and mention the recorded-role attribution in the staging sentence).

findings.what: Owner role derivation is less tolerant than seat attribution: the §3.3 fallback takes ownerRow.role whenever it is non-empty and does NOT try the CELL row's role when that spelling resolves to no roster role, while memberRoleOf (used for reuse and cap counting) tries row.role -> CELL role -> name base in order.
findings.where: packages/mpd-cellwork-plugin/src/elastic.ts — growExecutionSeats recordedRole selection (`typeof ownerRow.role === 'string' && ownerRow.role.trim() !== '' ? ownerRow.role : ownerCellRow?.role ?? ''`) vs memberRoleOf
findings.why: A live roster row carrying a non-roster role spelling (e.g. 'SE') blocks a growth pass the CELL row could have answered, even though the same seat is attributed correctly when it is a reuse candidate. The contract's 'first ... else ...' wording can be read as presence-order, so this is a latent edge, not a violation.
findings.direction: Derive the owner's role through the same spelling loop memberRoleOf uses (roster role, then CELL role), or share one helper for both derivations.

declined_to_judge: The unconditional `seat-grown` journal reason 'seat base came from the seat's recorded role' is inaccurate on a pass whose base resolved from the NAME — contract §3.5 explicitly requires that sentence, so it is not faulted.
TEAM `handoff.at` is written but currently consumed by nothing — contract §4.3 puts checkpointSinceOf plumbing and the force predicate out of scope.
CELL checkpointSince uses new Date() while the TEAM handoff.at uses deps.now(); under a fixed-clock harness the two stamps differ — contract §4.1 and §4.2 prescribe each source separately.

Reuse can pick a seat that the CALLER independently reassigns another row to in the same pass (growth does not read the caller's reassign targets) — pre-existing shape; contract §3.4 says reuse is paired 'exactly like today'.
memberRoleOf attributes a seat with no recorded role through its NAME base — the contract is silent on candidate attribution; it keeps older records attributable and is not contradicted by A1-A9.
maxPerRole counts verifier-only seats of the role (only planning seats are excluded) — the contract does not exclude verifier-only seats from the count.
The union of `reason` on the RESULT (owner-busy) vs the JOURNAL (recorded-role sentence) is asymmetric — contract §3.5 asks for exactly that split.
